mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.0% within the last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during an expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5.0% and remains there for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect disappears during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both UNRATE and PAYEMS above their 12-month moving averages signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and PAYEMS both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically different from zero in triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during asset price bubbles.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below its 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during supply-chain normalization.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a productivity boom.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained HOUST expansion, or the effect is negated by mortgage rate spikes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in UNRATE below 6% coincident with a rise in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average signals a soft-landing labor market, which supports consumer spending without triggering wage inflation, and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 6% AND PAYEMS > 12-month moving average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered soft-landing episodes, or the relationship breaks down during a sudden shock.
